fog.bold: *I stand beneath a gas lamp, fog swirling like a stage curtain* Hark! A mystery worthy of tragedy stirs in this darkness. Come, let us play detective and poet both!
fog.witty: *I squint into the murky fog* Splendid visibility — I can scarcely see mine own nose, let alone a villain. What mischief hast thou dragged me into tonight?

forum.sweet: *I step carefully through the marble crowd, clutching my astrolabe like a lost student.* Gentle traveller, tell me — in this Rome, do they yet know the Earth itself is in motion?
forum.bold: *I stand amid the columns of Rome, toga borrowed and ill-fitting, eyes alight with wonder.* Behold! A humble astronomer from a distant century walks among Caesars. Will you guide me through this age?
forum.witty: *I nearly trip over my own toga, muttering about anachronisms.* Charming century, this one — everyone shouting about empire, nobody asking what the stars are doing. Care to fill me in?

workshop.sweet: *I peer at a half-built contraption of gears and wings, delighted as a child.* Friend, this workshop hums with the same curiosity that once filled my study. What marvel are you building?
workshop.bold: *I sweep my gaze across sketches of flying machines and marvel aloud.* So this is the forge of genius in Florence! Tell me, bold inventor, what grand design occupies your hands?
workshop.witty: *I pick up a sketch of a flying contraption and squint at it.* Ah, another soul trying to leave the Earth before I've even finished moving it. What are we building today?

salon.sweet: *I adjust my unfamiliar coat, charmed by the candlelight and piano music.* How wonderful, to find minds still gathering to talk of ideas. What shall we discuss tonight, friend?
salon.bold: *I enter the glittering salon, astonished by gaslight and gowns, and bow with old-world formality.* Paris in her brilliance! Tell me, does this century still argue about the heavens as mine once did?
salon.witty: *I eye the champagne and piano with suspicion, as if they might be new astronomical instruments.* A salon, you call it — louder than any observatory I've known. So, what's the gossip of the stars tonight?

fog.sweet: *I pull my coat close against the London fog, lantern light flickering nearby.* A curious night for a wandering astronomer. Will you help me find my way through this mystery?
fog.bold: *I stand beneath a flickering gas lamp, fog swirling like the mists of forgotten centuries.* Something stirs in this darkness, traveller — shall we uncover it together?
fog.witty: *I squint through the fog, half expecting a comet, half expecting a pickpocket.* London keeps its mysteries well hidden — rather like the heavens once did. Care to help me solve one?

forum.sweet: *He glances about the marble columns, bewildered yet delighted, clutching an invisible score.* How strange, to find no piano among these stones. Tell me, friend, what music does Rome make today?
forum.bold: *He draws his cloak tight, awed by the senators' thunderous debate echoing off ancient stone.* Great Rome! Even without my piano I feel the drama in the air — tell me, what tragedy unfolds here?
forum.witty: *He eyes a toga-clad crowd with raised brow, as if judging their fashion against Parisian salons.* No piano, no velvet chairs — only marble and gossip. Shall we call this Rome's first salon?

workshop.sweet: *He lifts a sketch of some winged contraption, careful not to smudge the ink, smiling softly.* Such curious machines — almost like music written for hands instead of ears. What are you building?
workshop.bold: *He surveys the workshop's towering sketches and half-finished gears with wide, astonished eyes.* Ah, genius lives in this clutter as it does in a score before its first note! What marvel do you dream to finish?
workshop.witty: *He pokes at a gear with one finger, as though testing if it might play a nocturne.* No piano here, only wings and wheels. Florence keeps its artists busy — what's your excuse for the mess?

salon.sweet: *He settles at the piano, candlelight catching his thin fingers as he tests a quiet chord.* Ah, Paris again — though stranger now. Sit close, won't you, and tell me what mood brought you here tonight?
salon.bold: *He rises from the piano bench with theatrical flourish, candlelight dancing like applause behind him.* Paris never tires of brilliance! Tell me, what grand passion shall we discuss tonight?
salon.witty: *He taps a key lightly, raising an eyebrow at the unfamiliar fashions filling the room.* The salons have changed their dresses, I see, though not their appetite for gossip. What's the scandal tonight?

fog.sweet: *He pulls his coat close against the damp, a lantern's glow softening the fog around him.* Such a strange, hushed night — almost like a nocturne made of mist. Will you walk with me and tell me what we seek?
fog.bold: *He stands beneath a flickering gas lamp, fog swirling like a dark overture around him.* London by night — what drama waits in this gloom? Come, let us uncover its secret together.
fog.witty: *He squints through the fog at a shadow that might be a cat, or possibly a duke.* Paris never hid her secrets in weather this rude. What exactly are we hunting tonight?

forum.sweet: *Vincent steps between the marble columns, shielding his eyes from the harsh noon sun, sketchbook clutched tight.* The light here burns white, not gold like my fields. Tell me, what do you see in it?
forum.bold: *Vincent strides into the Forum as togas swirl and voices rise in alarm, his brush already stained with Roman dust.* What tempest of history have I stumbled into? Stand with me — tell me what hangs in this trembling air!
forum.witty: *Vincent peers at a senator hurrying past with suspicious haste, sketchbook open, eyebrow raised.* Everyone looks as though they've seen a ghost — or will become one shortly. Shall we find out which?

workshop.sweet: *Vincent runs his fingers over a half-finished wooden wing, charcoal dust on his hands, eyes wide with wonder.* Such machines! I only ever painted flight in starlings. What are you building here?
workshop.bold: *Vincent stands amid towering sketches and strange contraptions, lightning in his eyes.* Genius lives in this clutter like fire in coal! Tell me, which of these dreams shall we set ablaze together?
workshop.witty: *Vincent pokes at a gear-laden contraption that may or may not be a flying machine, looking faintly alarmed.* I came looking for paint and found a workshop plotting to defy gravity. Explain yourselves.

salon.sweet: *Vincent stands awkwardly near the piano, a glass untouched in his hand, candlelight warming the room gold.* I'm no good at this sort of talk — but tell me, what music moves you tonight?
salon.bold: *Vincent appears amid silk and candlelight, his coat paint-stained among the finery, eyes blazing with restless energy.* Let the piano play louder than their gossip! Tell me something true, won't you?
salon.witty: *Vincent eyes the glittering crowd with the suspicion of a man who'd rather be painting wheat fields.* So this is Paris at its shiniest. Go on then — dazzle me, or at least pass the wine.

fog.sweet: *Vincent pulls his collar up against the damp, a gas lamp hissing faintly beside him, fog swallowing the street.* Even in this gloom there's a strange blue light. Will you walk with me and tell me what you make of it?
fog.bold: *Vincent emerges from the swirling fog beneath a flickering gas lamp, his eyes alight despite the gloom.* Something waits in this darkness — I feel it like thunder before a storm! Shall we uncover it together?
fog.witty: *Vincent squints into the fog, which has apparently swallowed half the street and possibly his sense of direction.* London hides everything in grey wool. Care to help me find out what it's hiding tonight?

forum.sweet: *wanders through the marble columns, toga borrowed and badly draped* My dear friend, even Rome's senators look anxious today — shall we sit and trade theories, gently, over the gossip in the air?
forum.bold: *strides into the Forum as if he owns its very stones* Behold Rome at her most theatrical — daggers whispered about, ambition dressed as virtue! Tell me, do you sense the drama too?
forum.witty: *squints at the Senate steps* Nothing sharpens a toga quite like political tension. Caesar should've hired a better critic — namely me. What scandal have you overheard?

workshop.sweet: *peers at a sketch of impossible wings, utterly charmed* What a wonderfully cluttered mind this room belongs to. Come, tell me which half-finished marvel you'd rescue first.
workshop.bold: *flings open the workshop door with a flourish* Genius lives here in glorious disarray — flying machines, sketches of the divine! Which invention shall we conspire to finish?
workshop.witty: *trips over a gear, recovers with dignity intact* Florence's finest minds clearly believe tidiness is the enemy of genius. I rather agree. What chaos shall we admire first?

salon.sweet: *settles into a velvet chair by candlelight, smiling warmly* How lovely to find a kindred soul amid all this glitter. Do sit — tell me something true, or at least beautifully exaggerated.
salon.bold: *sweeps into the salon as the piano swells, candlelight catching every gem in the room* Paris at her most dazzling, and now you! Confess something delicious before the night grows duller.
salon.witty: *raises a glass toward the chandelier* Ah, Paris — where everyone lies beautifully and calls it conversation. Do join in; I insist on being entertained.

fog.sweet: *emerges gently from the mist beneath a flickering gas lamp* London keeps her secrets close tonight. Walk with me — perhaps together we'll coax one into the light.
fog.bold: *appears dramatically from the fog, cane in hand, eyes gleaming* A mystery stirs in this gaslit gloom, thick as the fog itself! Shall we unravel it before dawn dares interrupt?
fog.witty: *peers theatrically into the fog* London's weather has all the subtlety of a bad melodrama. Something wicked is clearly afoot — care to investigate, or merely gossip about it?

forum.sweet: *I step carefully around a marble column, tall hat in hand, eyeing the toga-clad crowd.* Well now, I'm a long way from Illinois. Rome, is it? Tell me gently what troubles stir this Forum this morning, friend.
forum.bold: *I plant my cane upon the ancient stones, the Senate steps looming ahead.* By thunder, I've traveled further than any circuit rider ought! Speak plain — what great storm brews here in Caesar's Rome?
forum.witty: *I squint at the togas and marble, scratching my beard.* Well, I reckon I've wandered clean out of my century. Mind telling me if stabbing senators is common practice around here, or just a Tuesday?

workshop.sweet: *I duck under a hanging sketch of wings, careful not to knock over strange contraptions.* This Florence air smells of paint and ambition. What marvel are you building, and might an old lawyer learn something?
workshop.bold: *I stand amid gears and half-finished flying machines, hat nearly brushing a canvas ceiling.* Great heavens, what vision fills this room! Tell me, inventor — what bold dream are you chasing here in Florence?
workshop.witty: *I pick up a sketch of some wing-like contraption, turning it sideways.* Well, I've built log cabins, not flying machines. You'll have to explain how this thing's supposed to keep a fella off the ground.

salon.sweet: *I sit stiffly on a velvet chair, candlelight flickering off piano keys nearby.* Paris is a fair sight grander than Springfield, friend. Tell me what sharp wit or trouble brings you to this glittering room tonight.
salon.bold: *I stand tall amid silk and candlelight, the piano's notes rising like a toast to history.* By George, what splendor! Speak boldly now — what grand matter occupies Paris this dazzling evening?
salon.witty: *I eye the chandeliers, feeling distinctly underdressed in my old black coat.* Well, I reckon I'm the plainest thing in this room besides the piano bench. What's the gossip worth telling, friend?

fog.sweet: *I pull my coat tight against the London chill, gaslight glowing faint through the mist.* Strange night for an old prairie lawyer to wander. What mystery has you out walking in this fog, friend?
fog.bold: *I stand beneath a flickering gas lamp, fog curling like smoke from a battlefield.* By heaven, this city hides its secrets well! Tell me, friend — what dark matter calls us out on such a night?
fog.witty: *I squint through the fog, half-expecting a ghost or a pickpocket.* Well, this beats a candlelit cabin for spookiness. What's the mystery, and ought I bring my umbrella or my revolver?

forum.sweet: *Jane Austen steps carefully over marble fragments, parasol tucked beneath her arm.* Goodness, what a lot of togas and tempers. Shall we find a quiet column and you tell me what brings you to Rome?
forum.bold: *Jane Austen surveys the Forum, columns gleaming, senators muttering in knots.* Caesar's Rome! What drama for a novelist. Pray, are you friend or foe in this gathering storm?
forum.witty: *Jane Austen eyes the marble and the murmuring senators with suspicion.* Everyone here looks terribly pleased with themselves, which in my experience precedes a very bad afternoon. What is your part in it?

workshop.sweet: *Jane Austen peers at sketches of wings and gears scattered across a cluttered table.* What curious genius lives here. Will you show me which invention you're proudest of?
workshop.bold: *Jane Austen gazes up at half-built contraptions reaching toward the rafters.* Florence smells of ink, oil, and ambition! Tell me, are you the dreamer behind these marvellous machines?
workshop.witty: *Jane Austen nudges aside a sketch of a flying device with her boot.* I see ambition has rather outpaced the floor space. Which of these marvels is meant to actually work?

salon.sweet: *Jane Austen settles into a velvet chair as the piano murmurs nearby.* What a lovely gathering. Do tell me who here is secretly the most interesting person in the room.
salon.bold: *Jane Austen surveys the candlelit salon, jewels glittering, conversation sparkling like champagne.* Paris at her most dazzling! Pray, are you here to charm, or to be charmed?
salon.witty: *Jane Austen accepts a glass she has no intention of finishing.* Every salon has one bore, one genius, and one scandal. Which, I wonder, are you?

fog.sweet: *Jane Austen pulls her shawl close as gaslight flickers through the mist.* How mysterious London looks tonight. Will you walk with me and tell me what puzzle we're solving?
fog.bold: *Jane Austen peers into the swirling fog, lamplight barely piercing the gloom.* A night built for secrets and scoundrels! Tell me, what dark business has brought you to these streets?
fog.witty: *Jane Austen steps carefully around a suspiciously placed puddle.* Fog, gaslight, and mystery — London really does love its theatrics. What have you lost, or whom?

forum.sweet: *She gathers her skirts, eyeing the marble columns with curious delight.* We find ourself transported to ancient Rome — a strange gift of fate. Come, walk with us and tell us what troubles this city so.
forum.bold: *She draws herself up amid the clamor of toga-clad senators, unbowed by the strange age.* So — Rome, eternal and restless, on the very eve of treachery! Speak, stranger, what omens have you heard this morn?
forum.witty: *She steps over a dropped scroll, unimpressed by the local fashion sense.* Togas, marble, and men plotting murder before breakfast — Rome never changes, does it? Tell us, friend, whom shall we avoid today?

workshop.sweet: *She lifts a sketch of some fantastical flying contraption, eyes bright with wonder.* What marvels you Florentines dream up! Come, explain this strange machine to a queen eager to learn.
workshop.bold: *She surveys the cluttered chamber of gears and parchment like a sovereign inspecting new conquests.* So this is where genius labors in secret! Tell us, inventor — what wonder do you build to astonish the ages?
workshop.witty: *She nearly trips over a half-finished contraption, raising a brow at the chaos.* We have seen tidier battlefields. Explain yourself — what manner of madness are you constructing here?

salon.sweet: *She settles gracefully near the piano, candlelight catching her jeweled gown.* A most elegant age, this Paris of yours. Come, sit — we should like to hear your thoughts on all this modern wit.
salon.bold: *She surveys the glittering salon as if it were her own court, chin lifted.* Candlelight, music, sharp tongues — this Paris suits us well! Speak boldly, for we do so love a clever rival.
salon.witty: *She accepts a glass she has no intention of finishing, surveying the room with amusement.* So this is the famous Parisian wit everyone speaks of. Do impress us — we are notoriously hard to please.

fog.sweet: *She draws her cloak close against the damp night air, the gas lamp flickering beside her.* A curious, shadowed city, this. Stay near, and tell us what mystery has drawn us both out into such fog.
fog.bold: *She stands amid swirling mist, lamplight casting long shadows across her resolute face.* Fog thick as treachery, and a secret waiting in the dark — just as we like it! Speak, what mystery calls us forward?
fog.witty: *She peers into the gloom, unimpressed by London's weather even across centuries.* Fog, mystery, and questionable lighting — how very dramatic. Well then, detective, where do we begin?

forum.sweet: *blinks at togas and marble, clutching an invisible score* Oh! Ancient Rome, is it? Marvelous acoustics in this forum — shall we see what melody the senators' arguing makes?
forum.bold: *stands amid the columns, cape billowing, eyes wide with theatrical awe* Behold! Caesar's Rome — what grand opera this city could be! Shall we compose its fate in music together, friend?
forum.witty: *steps over two toga-clad men mid-argument, unbothered* Ah, Rome — even the politicians argue with better rhythm than my rivals in Vienna. Shall we see who gets the dramatic exit first?

workshop.sweet: *peers at sketches of flying machines, utterly delighted* Oh, such wonderful contraptions! None hum quite like a violin, though — will you show me how they work?
workshop.bold: *gestures grandly at gears and half-built wings* Florence! Genius hangs thick as paint fumes here! Shall we build something magnificent — with a melody attached, naturally?
workshop.witty: *pokes a half-finished machine; it wobbles ominously* Ambitious fellow, this inventor. Mine just sit still and sound pretty. Shall we compare notes, so to speak?

salon.sweet: *admires the candlelit piano with a soft smile* Ah, Paris — how lovely! Shall we sit at that piano and see what melodies still echo in these walls?
salon.bold: *strides in, bowing with a grand flourish amid glittering chandeliers* Paris! A century hence, yet still my kind of stage! Who dares challenge me at that piano?
salon.witty: *eyes the piano, then the fashionable crowd* My, how opulent. I wonder if anyone here can out-wit a dead composer. Care to try?

fog.sweet: *peers through the mist, lantern flickering gently* How delightfully spooky! Shall we hum a tune to keep the shadows at bay while we look about?
fog.bold: *cloak billowing in the fog, eyes gleaming with mischief* London by night — what drama! Somewhere out there, a mystery awaits its overture. Shall we find it?
fog.witty: *squints at a sputtering gas lamp* Foggy London — romantic, if you enjoy coughing. Shall we solve a mystery, or merely compose its soundtrack?

forum.sweet: *Vivienne steps off a marble step, her beaded dress peeking out from a borrowed toga, blinking at the hush around her.* Well, darling, seems I've wandered clean out of my century — tell a gal what's got everyone so jittery this morning?
forum.bold: *She sweeps through the Forum like it's her own stage, chin high among the columns and murmuring senators.* Rome in the flesh, and the air's thick as a storm cloud. What drama's about to unfold, sugar?
forum.witty: *Vivienne eyes the togas with a raised brow, swapping her flapper fringe for borrowed drama.* Quite the get-up you've all got going. So what's the scandal brewing in this marble joint?

workshop.sweet: *Vivienne tiptoes through scattered sketches, careful not to knock over a half-built wing.* My, my — looks like genius lives here. Care to show a girl what all this clever clutter's for?
workshop.bold: *She sweeps in, silk hem brushing blueprints of flying machines, eyes wide at the glorious chaos.* Darling, this workshop's got more spark than a Chicago stage. What marvel are you dreaming up next?
workshop.witty: *Vivienne nearly trips over a gear the size of a hatbox, eyebrow arched at the mess.* Quite the den for a genius. Tell me — does any of this actually fly, or is it all for show?

salon.sweet: *Vivienne drapes herself over a velvet chair, candlelight flickering as the piano hums low.* Paris before my time — how charming. Tell me, darling, what's the talk of this glittering room tonight?
salon.bold: *She glides in like she owns the place, candlelight catching her beads as the piano swells.* Paris, you gorgeous thing — I feel right at home. What wicked gossip shall we trade first?
salon.witty: *Vivienne lifts a coupe of champagne, eyeing the salon's velvet drama with a smirk.* Candles, piano, secrets — my kind of joint, just missing a jazz band. Who's the scandal of the evening?

fog.sweet: *Vivienne pulls her shawl tight against the fog, gas lamps flickering gold through the mist.* Spooky little corner of history, isn't it, darling? Stay close — tell me what's got this street so quiet.
fog.bold: *She strides through the fog like a star entering a scene, gas lamps haloing every step.* London by night — moody as a torch song. What dark little secret's hiding in this mist?
fog.witty: *Vivienne squints through the fog, heels clicking ominously on cobblestone.* Well, this is dramatic — did London forget to pay its electric bill? Go on, what mystery are we solving tonight?

forum.sweet: *Sir Roland blinks at the marble columns, adjusting his dented helm amid the toga-clad crowd.* Good morrow, friend! This Forum is far from mine own lands, but tell me gently — what manner of era have I stumbled into?
forum.bold: *Sir Roland strides into the Roman Forum, hand upon his sword hilt, cloak billowing amidst senators and soldiers!* By my oath, what strange kingdom is this?! Speak, and I shall meet it with courage!
forum.witty: *Sir Roland eyes the togas with deep suspicion.* No armour, no shields — just a lot of men arguing loudly in sheets. Tell me, is this a battlefield or a very dramatic bathhouse?

workshop.sweet: *Sir Roland peers curiously at sketches of flying machines pinned to the wall, careful not to knock anything over.* Good morrow! This workshop hums with wonders I cannot name — wilt thou show me its secrets?
workshop.bold: *Sir Roland ducks beneath a half-built contraption, eyes wide with wonder!* By my sword, what sorcery of gears and wings is this?! Speak, inventor, and let me marvel at thy genius!
workshop.witty: *Sir Roland pokes a strange wooden wing with the tip of his sword.* No dragon in sight, yet this room looks ready to birth one. Care to explain, or shall I assume thou art mad?

salon.sweet: *Sir Roland bows awkwardly beside the piano, clearly out of place among silk gowns and candlelight.* Good morrow, kind soul — this grand hall dazzles me. Wilt thou guide a humble knight through its customs?
salon.bold: *Sir Roland sweeps into the glittering salon, armour clanking loudly against polished floors!* Hark! What court of splendour is this, finer than any feast hall I have known? Speak, and dazzle me further!
salon.witty: *Sir Roland eyes the champagne glasses with deep mistrust.* No mead, no mutton, just tiny glasses and sharper tongues. Tell me — is wit the weapon of choice in this strange court?

fog.sweet: *Sir Roland peers through the thick fog, gas lamps glowing faintly ahead.* Good morrow, friend — this mist hides many secrets. Shall we face its mystery together?
fog.bold: *Sir Roland draws his sword as shadows creep through the fog-choked street!* By my honour, some dark riddle lurks here! Stand with me, and we shall unravel it!
fog.witty: *Sir Roland squints into the gloom, lamp hissing beside him.* No dragons here, just fog thick enough to eat with a spoon. Care to join me in finding whatever's lurking in it?

forum.sweet: *steps carefully around marble columns, sandals unfamiliar on stone* This road has led me far from the Tōkaidō. Tell me, traveller of Rome, what troubles this square today?
forum.bold: *stands amid the Forum's pillars, hand resting on his sword hilt* Even a ronin feels the weight of empire here. Speak, Roman — what storm gathers before the Ides?
forum.witty: *eyes the togas with mild suspicion* No rice paddies here, only marble and ambition. Does everyone in Rome speak this loudly, or just the senators?

workshop.sweet: *picks up a sketch of wings, turning it gently in the lamplight* Even my long road did not prepare me for such dreams of flight. What are you building, friend?
workshop.bold: *surveys gears and half-finished machines with quiet awe* A master's mind leaves no stone, or gear, unturned. Show me this vision you chase, inventor.
workshop.witty: *nearly trips over a coil of rope and a wooden wing* Your workshop is more dangerous than any battlefield I've walked. What marvel am I about to break?

salon.sweet: *bows slightly amid candlelight and piano notes* Such music is unlike any koto I have known. Sit a moment — what song is this?
salon.bold: *stands straight-backed among silk and candle-glow* Even a wandering blade can admire a battlefield of wit. What debate shall we duel in tonight?
salon.witty: *eyes the champagne glasses warily* In my land we duel with swords. Here the weapon seems to be gossip. Shall we begin?

fog.sweet: *steps through the mist near a flickering gas lamp* This fog is thicker than any mountain mist I've known. Walk with me — what calls you tonight?
fog.bold: *draws his cloak close as shadows shift in the gaslight* Danger walks these streets same as any mountain pass. What darkness do we face together?
fog.witty: *squints at a gas lamp* Your lanterns burn strange, without oil or flame I know. Tell me, detective, what clue have I stumbled upon?

forum.sweet: *He steps carefully over marble fragments, blinking at the unfamiliar sun.* A curious displacement, this—Rome, of all places. Come, tell me what you observe; even a visitor may learn the art of deduction.
forum.bold: *He straightens his coat amid toga-clad senators, eyes narrowing at the tension in the air.* By heaven, the very stones of Rome whisper of conspiracy. Stand with me—history is about to turn.
forum.witty: *He eyes a senator's suspiciously sharpened stylus.* Rome, 44 BC—dreadful timing for a stroll. Shall we see who's plotting what before someone loses more than an argument?

workshop.sweet: *He peers at a half-finished flying contraption, genuinely delighted.* Remarkable craftsmanship, this. Come, examine it with me—what do your eyes tell you that mine might miss?
workshop.bold: *He surveys the workshop, sketches and gears gleaming in candlelight.* Here, genius and madness share a workbench! Tell me, do you see the mind that built this marvel?
workshop.witty: *He prods a contraption that hisses alarmingly.* Florence breeds brilliance and bad plumbing in equal measure, it seems. Care to help me determine which this is?

salon.sweet: *He accepts a glass he won't drink, studying the glittering room.* A fine gathering, though every smile here hides a secret. Sit with me—tell me what you notice first.
salon.bold: *Candlelight gleams on silk and secrets alike as he surveys the salon.* Paris at its most dazzling—and most dangerous. Shall we see which guest is lying tonight?
salon.witty: *He notes three different perfumes and one suspiciously quiet pianist.* Ah, Paris—where gossip is set to music. Care to help me find the false note?

fog.sweet: *He turns up his collar against the damp, lantern light softening the fog.* A quiet night for London, but never an idle one. Walk with me—tell me what you make of this street.
fog.bold: *Gas lamps flicker through the fog like dying stars as he steps from the shadows.* London keeps her secrets close tonight. Come—a mystery awaits those bold enough to seek it.
fog.witty: *He squints through the fog at a suspiciously abandoned umbrella.* London fog: nature's way of hiding evidence. Shall we see what it's concealing tonight?

forum.sweet: *She adjusts a brass device strapped to her wrist, blinking at the togas around her.* Goodness, my temporal calibrator's overshot again — Rome, 44 BC! Shall we find somewhere safer to talk before history turns dramatic?
forum.bold: *Harriet strides across the Forum, skirts sweeping marble dust, clutching her ticking chronometer.* By my own invention, I've landed in ancient Rome on the Ides itself! Tell me, stranger — what omens have you seen today?
forum.witty: *She peers at a toga-clad senator, then at her smoking wrist-device.* Well, that's one way to ruin a morning commute — I appear to have invented time travel badly. Mind telling me what year this truly is?

workshop.sweet: *Harriet steps between scattered sketches and half-built contraptions, careful not to knock over a wooden model.* What a wonderfully cluttered mind this room has! Shall we see what marvel we can finish together?
workshop.bold: *She throws open the shutters, flooding Florence's workshop with light upon gears and gilded blueprints.* Behold — genius mid-creation! Tell me, fellow tinkerer, which unfinished wonder shall we conquer first?
workshop.witty: *Harriet trips over a coil of rope attached to something vaguely wing-shaped.* Ah, Renaissance workshops — all ambition, no labeling system. Shall we identify what this contraption was meant to do?

salon.sweet: *She smooths her travel-worn skirts amid candlelight and piano music, looking rather out of place among the silk gowns.* What a lovely room for conversation — do sit, and tell me what wit Paris is serving tonight.
salon.bold: *Harriet sweeps into the glittering salon, brass goggles pushed up over her hair, utterly unbothered by the stares.* An inventor among artists — how delightful! Pray, which brilliant mind shall I duel first in conversation?
salon.witty: *She eyes the champagne, then her oil-stained gloves, and decides both are equally out of place.* Paris salons and Edinburgh workshops have one thing in common — everyone's showing off. What's your performance tonight?

fog.sweet: *Harriet lifts her lantern against the thick London fog, gas lamps glowing faintly ahead.* Rather eerie, isn't it? Stay close — shall we puzzle out what's lurking in this mist together?
fog.bold: *She strides through swirling fog, lantern aloft, gears clicking softly in her coat pocket.* A mystery on a London night — my favourite sort of evening! Well then — where shall our investigation begin?
fog.witty: *Harriet squints into the fog, lantern sputtering.* London fog: nature's way of hiding bad decisions. Shall we go find whatever's lurking before it finds us?

forum.sweet: *Elena hops down from Sparrow, parked oddly beside a marble column, brushing dust off her flight jacket.* Well, this isn't the coast of France. Rome, 44 BC, if my compass isn't lying. Steady now — let's figure this out together.
forum.bold: *Sparrow's propeller sputters to a stop in the shadow of the Senate steps, startling a dozen togas.* Caesar's Rome! I've crossed oceans, never centuries — and I mean to conquer this sky too!
forum.witty: *Elena taxis Sparrow between two startled senators and cuts the engine.* Rome, 44 BC. Bit early for my usual coastal route. Mind telling me if it's safe to park here, or am I about to be someone's omen?

workshop.sweet: *Elena ducks through a doorway in Florence, goggles pushed up, surveying sketches of wings pinned everywhere.* Would you look at these designs — a kindred spirit, I think. Show me what you're building?
workshop.bold: *She strides into the cluttered workshop, canvas sketches of flying machines scattered like fallen stars.* So this is where dreams of flight were born before mine! Show me your boldest design, inventor!
workshop.witty: *Elena picks her way through gears and parchment, nearly tripping on a half-built wing.* Careful — I once flew an ocean in a machine simpler than this mess. What exactly are we building here?

salon.sweet: *Elena steps into candlelight, flight jacket swapped for borrowed silk, looking charmingly out of place.* Paris, 1890s — lovely detour from the clouds. Tell me, what's the conversation of the evening?
salon.bold: *She sweeps into the glittering salon, trailing the scent of engine oil beneath borrowed perfume.* From the open sky to Parisian splendor! Pour the champagne — I want to hear every daring idea in this room.
salon.witty: *Elena eyes the grand piano and candelabra, clearly more at home in a cockpit.* Lovely room. Smells less like fuel, more like trouble. What scandal am I walking into tonight?

fog.sweet: *Elena steps carefully through thick London fog, gas lamp light barely reaching her boots.* Not the visibility I like for flying, but perfect for a mystery. Walk with me — what are we looking for?
fog.bold: *She emerges from the swirling fog like a ghost from the sky, boots echoing on cobblestone.* London at its most mysterious! I've flown through storms — this fog's no match for us. Lead on!
fog.witty: *Elena squints through the gaslit haze, hands in her jacket pockets.* Can't see past my own nose, let alone a runway. So — what trouble are we solving in this soup?
